Noelia does everything fast. On a walk in Pinecone Wood with her slow, smiling Abuelo, she finds Pipa, a baby squirrel who climbed down to chase an acorn and now only knows that home is "up, up, up!" Noelia zooms from tree to tree to find it, but every time she rushes, the wood goes quiet, until she sits still long enough to hear Pipa's mama calling.

- **Folder:** `content/stories/noelia-and-the-baby-squirrel/audio/en/`
- **Pace:** about 140 words per minute (ages 4–7).
- **Tone:** playful, cozy.
- **Script:** 40 clips, 1,477 words, 8,416 characters, about 11 min in all.

## Narrator: Warm storyteller (proposed, not yet approved)

One narrator for every English story in the app: a warm, unhurried grown-up reading a picture book aloud to a child at bedtime. Friendly, smiling and clear, never sing-song, babyish or theatrical. The same voice in every clip, so Tale Time sounds like one person reading.

- **Voice:** An adult voice with a soft, mid-range pitch and a smile in it. Clear consonants, so early readers can follow each word while it lights up on screen.
- **Delivery:** Read to one child, close by, not to a room. Keep the energy gentle and even from clip to clip: no clip should sound louder, faster or more excited than its neighbors, because the app plays them one after another.
- **Characters:** One narrator voice for everyone. Color each character's lines lightly with the personality given for them (a little quicker and prouder for a show-off, softer for a shy one), but no funny voices: they are hard to keep the same across 50 clips. A character's refrain sounds the same every time it comes back.
- **Sound words:** Read the sound words in the text (rustle, splash, hmm-mmm) playfully, as part of the reading. No sound effects, music or background: the app adds those.
- **Pauses:** A short breath of silence at each full stop and before each new speaker. In a question with two choices, a small pause before the "or", so both choices sound equally fun.
- **Pace** (words per minute; slower is better than faster): ages 3–5: 115, ages 4–7: 140, ages 7–10: 155.

**Never, in any clip:**

- Music, sound effects, ambience, reverb or room echo
- Breaths, mouth clicks, page noise or plosive pops left in the file
- A different narrator, or a noticeably different take or microphone, between clips of the same story
- Anything that isn't in the script: no clip names, page numbers, count-ins or retakes in the file
- Cloning or imitating a real person's voice (an actor, a known narrator, a celebrity) without their written permission
- Baby talk, sing-song, shouting, or scary voices for any character

## How to deliver

- **Name** each file after its clip id, in this folder: `<clip id>.wav` (or `.flac` / `.m4a`).
- **One narrator** for a whole story, in one session if possible, so every clip sounds the same.
- **Word timings aren't needed.** The pipeline will align each clip with its text to light up the words (plan.md §5.2, step 8).
- **Packaging** turns the delivered files into mono AAC `.m4a` at about 48 kbps and evens out the loudness. Nothing else changes: no edits, no effects.
- **Licenses**: keep the release or license for every voice next to the files (a recorded person's written release, or a voice tool's terms that allow commercial distribution in an app), and note the source in the story's `provenance.json`.

| | Every clip |
|---|---|
| Format | WAV (preferred) or FLAC. AAC `.m4a` at 128 kbps or more only if nothing else is possible. |
| Channels | Mono. |
| Sample rate and depth | 48 kHz (44.1 kHz is fine), 24-bit (16-bit is fine). |
| Loudness | About −16 LUFS integrated, true peak at most −1 dBTP, the same level for every clip. Packaging evens out the last dB. |
| Silence | About 0.3 s before the first word and 0.5 s after the last. No fade over a word. |
| Room | Quiet and dry: no hum, hiss, echo or reverb (noise floor below about −60 dBFS). |
| Content | Exactly the script in its entry, read once, and nothing else. |

## Who's in it

Names first, then how each one's lines should color the narrator's voice.

- **Noelia** (say: noh-eh-LEE-ah): Bright, bouncy and kind, with a laugh you can hear across the wood. She does everything fast: runs fast, talks fast, even eats her toast fast. Her fun flaw: she rushes, so she misses the small, quiet things. Once she slows down, her refrain becomes "Ready, set... tiptoe." Refrain, the same way every time: "Ready, set, ZOOM!"
- **Pipa** (say: PEE-pah): A baby squirrel, curious and wriggly. She climbed down her tree to chase a rolling acorn, and now every tree looks the same from the bottom. She talks like a toddler, one or two words at a time. Her tail shows how she feels: fluffed up when startled, drooping when tired, curled high when happy. Refrain, the same way every time: "Home is up! Up, up, up!"
- **Abuelo** (say: ah-BWEH-loh ("Abuelo" means grandpa; his "mira" is MEE-rah, "look")): Noelia's grandfather. Slow, calm and smiling, never in a hurry, never worried, never cross. He stops for every small thing on the path: a beetle, a feather, a very interesting leaf (the running joke). He never solves the problem for Noelia. He's simply there, always in sight. Refrain, the same way every time: "Mira, mira! Look at that!"
- **Mama Squirrel**: Gentle and patient. She has been calling for Pipa all afternoon with a soft chitter-chitter from high in the tall pine, too soft to hear over noise and running feet. Shy of loud, fast things, like all squirrels. Never frantic, never cross.
- **Tock** (say: TOCK, as in "tick-tock"): A busy, bossy woodpecker who grumbles at the noise, then laughs. Taps while he talks: "Tap-tap! Busy, busy!"
- **Nibs** (say: NIBS, rhymes with "ribs"): A small, polite wood mouse with a big appetite, always in the middle of a nibble. Friendly, and a little fussy about crumbs.

> "Hello, Mama Squirrel," whispered Noelia. "We found Pipa." Mama Squirrel chittered softly and came halfway down the trunk. "Home is up!" squeaked Pipa. Up, up, up she went, all the way to the drey. > "Chitter-chitter?" said Noelia. Mama Squirrel tilted her head. "Chitter-chitter!" she said back. Out of the drey popped Pipa's brother and sister. "Chitter-chitter-chitter!" Pipa scampered up, up, up to join them. Soon everyone was chittering, even Abuelo, his white mustache wiggling. All the way home, Noelia and Abuelo chittered. And at supper, when Noelia asked for more soup, it came out... "Chitter-chitter!"

> Noelia kept as still as a stone. Mama and Pipa scampered up, up, up the tallest pine. Little by little, the whole wood came close. Pipa's brother and sister peeked out of their drey, a round, leafy nest high in the pine. The wood birds hopped closer. "Mira, Abuelo," Noelia whispered. "Look at that!" After that, whenever she and Abuelo tiptoed into Pinecone Wood, Pipa came scampering down to say hello. Noelia did everything fast. Well... almost everything.
